chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd, from some of our companions, who said:

I was with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام on the road to Makkah. We came to a well, and the servant of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام drew a bucket, and two mice came out in it. So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Pour it out.” He said: Then he drew another, and a mouse came out in it. So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “Pour it out.” He said: Then he drew a third, and nothing came out in it, so he said: “Pour it into the vessel.” So he poured it into the vessel.

So the first point in this hadith is that ʿAlī ibn Ḥadīd narrated it from some of our companions and did not provide a complete sanad/isnad for it, and this is among the things that weaken the hadith. Even if it is accepted, it is possible that by “well” he meant a reservoir in which there was water whose amount exceeded the measure of a kurr, in which case drawing out any amount from it would not be obligatory. Then he did not say that he performed wudu (ablution) from it; rather, he said: “Pour it into the vessel,” and in his saying “Pour it into the vessel” there is no indication of the permissibility of using it for wudu (ablution). It is also possible that he only ordered him to pour it into the vessel because they needed it for drinking, and this is permissible according to us in cases of necessity.

Then al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If a camel dies in it, all that is in it is to be drawn out. If that is difficult due to the abundance and profusion of the water, then four men should alternate in drawing from it from the beginning of the day to its end, and by that it has become purified. If khamr falls into it—and that is an intoxicating drink, from whichever kinds it may be—then all that is in it is to be drawn out if it is little; and if it is much, then four men should alternate in drawing it out from the beginning of the day to its end, according to what we have mentioned. The proof for that is that when a camel falls into the water, or khamr, then the water has become impure without disagreement. Therefore, it is obligatory that it not be judged pure except by decisive proof, and there is no proof in the Shari'ah that establishes any fixed amount decisively, so it is obligatory that all of it be drawn out. This is also further supported.

key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: necessity that permits otherwise restricted use
key_terms.بَعِيرٌ: a camel whose death in the well causes severe contamination
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well from which water is drawn
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: intoxicating drink causing impurity in the water
key_terms.فَأْرَةٌ: a mouse found in the drawn water
key_terms.نُزِحَ: drawn out or drained from the well

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about purifying well water contaminated by dead animals or khamr?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a report about water drawn from a well in which mice appeared, followed by the author's legal analysis of the report and its weakness in sanad/isnad. It then presents juristic rulings concerning the purification of well water when contaminated by a dead camel or khamr, emphasizing the need for complete draining or sustained drawing based on the severity and amount.
